--- title: "Evaluation" description: "Measure a function on rows with known answers: a score with its interval, a table of every answer, and paired comparisons." --- A prompt that looks right on three examples can be wrong on the fourth. The only way to know how well a function works is to run it on examples with known answers and count. `functai.evaluate` does that, and gives you the score *with its uncertainty*, and every answer as a table to dig into. Tables come from [dpyr](https://github.com/MaximeRivest/dpyr) (dplyr's verbs, in Python, over polars and duckdb): `pip install "functai[data]"`. ## Data is rows A list of dictionaries, or any table: a CSV or parquet file, a pandas or polars dataframe, a Hugging Face dataset. Columns named like the function's **parameters** are its inputs. A column named like an **output** is the expected answer (`result` for the return value). Any other column is kept, to group or filter by later. The support desk from [Get started](../get-started.qmd) routes each message to a team. It has two house rules the model can't guess: an item that arrives broken is a **shipping** claim (the carrier pays), and anything about money back is **billing**. ::: {#e61d0316 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from typing import Literal @ai def category(message: str) -> Literal["shipping", "billing", "product", "account"]: """The support category of the message.""" dev = [ {"message": "The mug arrived in pieces.", "result": "shipping", "channel": "email"}, {"message": "I want my money back for the toaster, it's useless.", "result": "billing", "channel": "chat"}, {"message": "The kettle's lid doesn't close properly.", "result": "product", "channel": "email"}, {"message": "How do I change the email on my profile?", "result": "account", "channel": "chat"}, {"message": "Box was crushed and the lamp inside is cracked.", "result": "shipping", "channel": "email"}, {"message": "Please refund the blender, it stopped working.", "result": "billing", "channel": "chat"}, {"message": "Toaster burns one side of the bread.", "result": "product", "channel": "chat"}, {"message": "Please delete my account and my data.", "result": "account", "channel": "email"}, {"message": "Screen was shattered when I opened the package.", "result": "shipping", "channel": "chat"}, {"message": "Return the headphones and give me a refund please.", "result": "billing", "channel": "email"}, {"message": "Tracking hasn't moved in a week.", "result": "shipping", "channel": "email"}, {"message": "My coupon code didn't apply at checkout.", "result": "billing", "channel": "chat"}, ] ``` ::: ## A score, and how sure it is ::: {#0a5d930a .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} ev = functai.evaluate(category, dev, num_threads=8) ev ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Evaluation(category, 12 examples: exact_match 0.58 [0.32, 0.81]) ``` ::: ::: With no metric given, the score is exact match against the `result` column (ignoring case and spacing). **The interval is the part to read.** On 12 examples the true accuracy could be anywhere in it; on 30 examples, 80% still means "somewhere between 63% and 90%". Collect more examples before you trust a small difference. `ev.summary` has one row per metric: ::: {#716ac8fa .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} ev.summary ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
# dpyr · source: polars · showing 1 of 1 rows
metricmeanlowhighnfailed

"exact_match"0.5833330.3195110.80674120
``` ::: ::: ## Every answer, as a table `ev.table` has one row per example: the data, the prediction (`pred_result`), each metric, the error if the row failed, the time and the tokens it took. Because it is a table, the usual data tools apply. The misses: ::: {#f6f2dc25 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} from dpyr import col, n ev.table.filter(col.exact_match == 0).select(col.message, col.result, col.pred_result) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
# dpyr · source: polars · showing 5 of 5 rows

"Return the headphones and give me a refund please.""billing""product"

Accuracy by category, and by the channel the message came from: ::: {#fcfc04ee .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} ev.table.group_by(col.result).summarize(accuracy=col.exact_match.mean(), n=n()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: `ev.write("today.parquet")` saves it; `ev.table.collect()` gives a polars dataframe. ## Metrics A metric scores one row. It can be: - **a function** `metric(row, prediction) -> float | bool`: the row as a dict, the prediction with attribute access; - **a dpyr expression** over the table's columns, computed on the whole table at once: `col.pred_result == col.result`; - **an AI function**, acting as a judge (one model call per row). Use a judge when "right" can't be checked by code: a summary, a translation, a reply's tone. Give several as a dict; the first is the one `ev.score` reports. ::: {#f1781c53 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} @ai def plausible(row: dict, prediction: dict) -> float: """Between 0 and 1: could a reasonable support agent have chosen the predicted category for this message, even if it is not the expected one?""" ev2 = functai.evaluate(category, dev, { "exact": col.pred_result == col.result, "not_account": lambda row, pred: pred.result != "account", "plausible": plausible, }, num_threads=8) ev2.summary ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}
# dpyr · source: polars · showing 3 of 3 rows
metricmeanlowhighnfailed
strf64f64f64i64i64
"exact"0.5833330.3195110.80674120

Problems that would waste a whole run (a missing input column, a metric with the wrong signature) are refused before any model is called. ## Comparing two versions The misses showed the model doesn't know the house rules, so state them in the docstring, and compare the two versions **on the same examples**. `compare` pairs them row by row, which detects a real change with far fewer examples than two separate scores would: ::: {#3a936d99 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} @ai def category_v2(message: str) -> Literal["shipping", "billing", "product", "account"]: """The support category of the message. House rules: an item that arrived broken is shipping (the carrier pays), and any request for money back is billing.""" after = functai.evaluate(category_v2, dev, num_threads=8) functai.compare(ev, after) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ```{=html}
# dpyr · source: polars · showing 1 of 1 rows
metricbeforeafterdifflowhighbetterworsesamen
strf64f64f64f64f64i64i64i64i64
"exact_match"0.5833331.00.4166670.0894940.74383950712
``` ::: ::: `better`, `worse` and `same` count examples that changed. `low` and `high` bound the difference: when they include 0, the change could be luck, and the honest next step is more examples. ## Keeping a record `evaluate(..., log="runs/")` writes each run to `runs/.parquet`, and `functai.runs("runs/")` reads all of them back as one table: every version you tried, side by side.
